claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know that Alex is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or do you have the right to reside in the UK in another way?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen living here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that. That helps with the residency requirements.

Now, I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you the only person claiming or intending to claim Child Benefit for Alex, or is someone else also responsible for Alex's care and upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm the only one - no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that.

Now I have a clearer picture. Let me ask one more important question to confirm your eligibility:

**Are you living with Alex and responsible for their day-to-day care, or are you paying towards Alex's upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money, or housing) even if Alex lives with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me and I'm responsible for all their day-to-day care - everything from meals to clothes to getting them to school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and upkeep
- You are a British citizen with the right to reside in the UK
- You are the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You meet all the key eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. You are normally entitled to claim Child Benefit as you are responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK.

**Please note:** There is also a High Income Child Benefit tax charge that may apply if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000. You can use the Child Benefit tax calculator on the UK government website to check if this would affect you, but this doesn't prevent you from being eligible to claim.
